stemMd: Which line is perpendicular to y = −2x + 5 and passes through (4,1)?
explanationMd: Perpendicular nonvertical lines have slopes whose product is −1. The required slope is 1/2. In point-slope form y − 1 = (x − 4)/2, giving y = x/2 − 1.

distractorRationale.a: This is parallel to the given line.
distractorRationale.e: Its slope is the negative of the original, not the negative reciprocal.
distractorRationale.d: Its slope has the wrong sign for perpendicularity.
distractorRationale.b: This has the right slope but misses the point (4,1).
